You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– likely-relevant recent bug reports,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.
Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Diagnosis:
The test `testEscapedQuote_LANG_477` uses a pattern with escaped single quotes: "it''s a {0,lower} 'test'!". This pattern includes both doubled single quotes (to represent a literal single quote character) and quoted strings ('test'). The failing bug report states that using ExtendedMessageFormat with a custom format registry and a pattern containing single quotes causes an OutOfMemoryError.

Looking at the code, ExtendedMessageFormat.applyPattern(String pattern) is the method that parses the pattern. The method iterates through the characters of the pattern using a ParsePosition and switches on whether the character is a quote (case QUOTE), a format start (case START_FE), or other characters.

When it encounters a quote (case QUOTE), it calls appendQuotedString, which processes quoted substrings in the pattern. This method manages single quotes carefully, including handling escaped quotes (two consecutive single quotes).

In appendQuotedString, the code checks if escaping is on and if the current character is a quote, then it appends a quote and moves forward. It then iterates through the pattern characters, appending character sequences between quotes and handling escaped quotes (two single quotes in a row) by appending a single quote. If a quoted string is not properly terminated (missing closing quote), an IllegalArgumentException is thrown.

The problem is likely that in the presence of a custom format registry, when processing a pattern with single quotes, the parsing does not properly advance the ParsePosition or consume the quotes, possibly causing an infinite loop or indefinite accumulation in the pattern processing loop in applyPattern. This leads to an OutOfMemoryError because the while loop continues indefinitely processing the pattern.

In summary, the infinite loop causing OutOfMemoryError is triggered by how applyPattern and appendQuotedString handle quoted strings and escaped quotes, especially when using a custom format registry. The pattern string is not properly consumed/advanced in the case of single quotes, so parse position does not move forward leading to an endless loop in applyPattern.

The root cause is that appendQuotedString may return without advancing ParsePosition when encountering escaped quotes in some scenarios, or that applyPattern's main loop incorrectly handles quoted strings by not advancing position or appending properly, causing it to never terminate when single quotes and custom registry coexist.

This explains why OutOfMemoryError arises only with a custom format registry (registration adds complexity in parseFormatDescription and getFormat) and the pattern containing single quotes.

Recent bug reports retrieved are unrelated; they focus on equals/hashCode implementations for BigDecimal objects and don't involve pattern parsing or format handling in ExtendedMessageFormat.

Hence, the bug lies in ExtendedMessageFormat.applyPattern and appendQuotedString handling of quoted strings with single quotes and custom format registry.

Next step would be to inspect the code that advances the ParsePosition inside these methods and how the loop conditions depend on pos.getIndex() advancing, confirming the infinite loop scenario.
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test uses a pattern with escaped single quotes and quoted strings, which triggers ExtendedMessageFormat to parse these quoted strings. The core parsing loop in ExtendedMessageFormat.applyPattern uses a ParsePosition to iterate through the pattern. When encountering single quotes, it calls appendQuotedString to parse the quoted substring or escaped quotes.

appendQuotedString is expected to consume the quoted substring and advance the ParsePosition accordingly, returning the processed string fragment. However, with a custom format registry involved, the looping logic in applyPattern seemingly doesn't advance the ParsePosition correctly for certain quoted string patterns. This causes the main while loop in applyPattern to never terminate, leading to continuous appending to the StringBuffer and eventually an OutOfMemoryError.

Recent unrelated bug reports about equals/hashCode implementations for BigDecimal do not connect to this issue.

Thus, the root cause is that ExtendedMessageFormat.applyPattern, in conjunction with appendQuotedString, mishandles single-quoted substrings when a custom format registry is set, failing to advance the ParsePosition properly and causing an infinite loop and memory exhaustion when parsing patterns with single quotes.

The faulty methods responsible are ExtendedMessageFormat.applyPattern and appendQuotedString.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
